title: Current mirror: ratios and output resistance

sections.heading: The idea
sections.body_md:
A **current mirror** copies a reference current. A diode-connected device turns \(I_{REF}\) into a gate voltage. A second device with the same gate and source sees the same \(V_{GS}\) and therefore carries the same current density. Its output current is \(I_{REF}\) scaled by the ratio of the two \(W/L\) values. Mobility, oxide capacitance and threshold are shared by matched devices, so they cancel, and the ratio is set by geometry, which layout controls well. One reference can feed a whole bus of outputs with different ratios.

The copy is only good while the output device is **saturated**, so the output must stay above \(V_{ov}\). Two non-idealities matter. Channel-length modulation makes the output current depend on its own \(V_{DS}\). If the output sits at a different drain voltage from the reference, the current is off by the ratio \((1 + \lambda V_{DS2})/(1 + \lambda V_{DS1})\). For the same reason the mirror's small-signal output resistance is just \(r_{o2}\).

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md: \[ I_{OUT} = \frac{(W/L)_2}{(W/L)_1}I_{REF}\cdot\frac{1 + \lambda V_{DS2}}{1 + \lambda V_{DS1}}, \qquad R_{out} = r_{o2} = \frac1{\lambda I_{OUT}}, \qquad V_{out,\min} = V_{ov} \]

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md: A reference device with \(W/L = 3\) carries \(30\ \mu\mathrm{A}\) at \(V_{DS} = 0.7\ \mathrm{V}\). An output device with \(W/L = 12\) gives a nominal \(120\ \mu\mathrm{A}\). With \(\lambda = 0.08\ \mathrm{V^{-1}}\) and the output at 1.2 V, it actually carries \(120(1.096/1.056) \approx 124.5\ \mu\mathrm{A}\). Its output resistance is about \(1/(0.08\cdot124.5\ \mu\mathrm{A}) \approx 100\ \mathrm{k\Omega}\).

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md:
- Letting the output fall below \(V_{ov}\), which sends the device into triode.
- Ignoring the \(\lambda\) error when the two drains sit at different voltages.
- Scaling by \(W\) alone when the lengths differ.

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: Mirrors bias everything: tails of differential pairs, current-source loads, references. Cascoding them raises \(R_{out}\), and a PMOS mirror makes an active load.
